attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in the first person.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the $450B+ annual revenue expectation, the exclusion of the two 'oafs' (OpenAI and Anthropic, per the surrounding text) and 'a few billion'. 'I believe' states his view and is not on the policy's list of hedges, so this is a scorable observation about the present.

contract.note: The plain reading (a snapshot at publication; revenue treated as an estimate; no demand interval imposed) is ordinary and fair. It sensibly refuses to let hardware sales, total cloud revenue or multiyear commitments settle the claim on their own.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's expectation of about $1T in hardware sales through 2027 is cumulative chip sales, not annual revenue to data-center operators. It does not test the $450B figure.
The Nebius–Meta deal (up to $27B over five years, starting 2027) is future, multiyear and partly a backstop. It is not current demand on any stated basis.
Epoch's estimate (OpenAI and Anthropic at 15–20% of operational compute, end of 2025) measures physical compute at an earlier date, not current dollar demand. It is suggestive but not comparable.

reviews.rationale: Neither side of the comparison is measured at publication. No item ties capacity being built to $450B+ in annual revenue. No item gives a comparable dollar figure for current demand excluding OpenAI and Anthropic. The Meta deal and the Epoch estimate hint at larger outside demand, but they cover future commitments or earlier physical compute, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will' with the trigger 'once demand wanes… after hyperscalers reduce their capex' is a firm conditional forecast. The chain (ODMs, then RAM and storage, then a prolonged depression) and the no-bailout assertion are kept in his order. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Requiring the trigger first, reading 'kill' as severe declines, and treating 'no bailout' as categorical are ordinary readings. Growth before the trigger correctly does not count against the forecast.

evidence.note: TrendForce (Aug 3) reports stronger procurement of NVIDIA rack systems and rising cloud-provider capex. This bears on the trigger not having occurred, not on the outcome of the forecast.
NVIDIA's CFO (Aug 26) describes accelerating demand. This is a company disclosure about the trigger, not evidence of the outcome.
J.P. Morgan's projection of AI capex near $1T for 2026 is forward-looking and does not establish whether actual capex was cut.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet does not show the trigger (industry-wide capex cuts followed by weaker NVIDIA GPU demand). Evidence through August points to strengthening demand. With the trigger unmet, the forecast is not scored, and no triggered episode or bailout has been observed.
